summary.oneLiner: Suprajit crossed INR 1,000 cr quarterly revenue with consolidated PBT doubling YoY, driven by the successful EBITDA turnaround of acquired SCS and global restructuring. FY27 guidance targets double-digit revenue growth and 12-13.5% EBITDA margins, leveraging operational fixes in Mexico/Europe and new wins in EV electronics and braking systems.

one-line thesis: Suprajit crossed INR 1,000 cr quarterly revenue with consolidated PBT doubling YoY, driven by the successful EBITDA turnaround of acquired SCS and global restructuring. FY27 guidance targets double-digit revenue growth and 12-13.5% EBITDA margins, leveraging operational fixes in Mexico/Europe and new wins in EV electronics and braking systems.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,000+ cr (Q4 run-rate), Full Year +17% YoY; EBITDA: +19-20% YoY, Margin ~13.1% (Op. EBITDA INR 443 cr); PAT: Consolidated PBT INR 97 cr (Q4, ~2x YoY), Standalone PBT lower than Consolidated for first time post-LDC/SCS; Order Book: Strong double-digit growth in India/China (specific value undisclosed); Net Debt: INR 550 cr (Gross Debt INR 785 cr less Cash/MF INR 235 cr). One-offs: SCS restructuring costs absorbed; Tariff recoveries ongoing but not fully recognized in FY26 margins.
guidance: Revenue: Double-digit growth FY27; Margin: 12%-13.5% Consolidated EBITDA (GCM specifically guided 10%-12%); Order Inflow: Strong wins in EV clusters, throttle controls, and US retailer; Capex: INR 200 cr allocated.
order book & pipeline: Strong double-digit growth in India and China operations; Specific monetary value undisclosed but described as 'strong' with new wins in premium EV motorbikes and US off-highway.
segment / subsidiary detail: GCM (ex-SCD+SCS): Revenue +10% (ex-SCS), Margin improved to 11% (ex-SCS), SCS turned EBITDA positive (+2% in Q4); ICM (ex-DCD): Revenue +9% (impacted by price concessions), underlying volume strong, margins robust; SED: Revenue +20%, strong momentum in digital clusters/throttle controls; PLE (ex-PLD): Revenue -3%, margin pressure from commodity costs and Middle East conflict affecting TRIFA brand.
growth verticals / optionality: Beyond-Cables: Brake calipers (TCA signed), Sunroof cables, ABS (with Bluebrake); EV Electronics: Complete clusters/throttle/switch assembly for premium EV bikes; US Retailer channel expansion for electrical products; Market share gains from insolvent global halogen competitor.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 margin pressure from commodity inflation (Moly, Tungsten) and lagged price concessions in India; FY27 margin expansion (400 bps for GCM) driven by operational restructuring (factory consolidation in Mexico, warehouse shifts in Europe) and full-year contribution of turned-around SCS; Tariff recoveries expected to be fully realized.
capex / expansion: INR 200 cr planned: INR 80 cr India ops (incl. Chennai Plant-2, AURIC land), INR 50 cr Global ops, INR 50 cr Tech Center (STC building), INR 15-16 cr Corporate/IT; Includes INR 30-40 cr over 2 years for new Electronics division building.
capital allocation: Dividend increased to INR 3.50/share (from INR 3.00); Debt reduction prioritized (Net Debt INR 550 cr); Strategic M&A integration complete (SCS, LDC); Focus on sweating assets in Lighting division.
risks & watch-items: Middle East geopolitical conflict impacting supply chain and TRIFA sales; Commodity price volatility (Moly, Tungsten) if pass-through fails; Customer project launch delays; Tariff regulation changes.
management quality / tone: Confident and decisive; Emphasis on 'heavy lifting' of restructuring being complete; Pragmatic on external risks (Middle East, commodities); Strategic shift from 'cable player' to 'mechatronics/solutions' provider.
non-obvious takeaways: Consolidated PBT exceeded Standalone PBT for the first time, marking a structural shift in earnings mix towards global subsidiaries; Renaming of divisions (DCD->ICM, SCD->GCM, PLD->PLE) signals strategic pivot to mechatronics and electricals beyond pure cables; 'Last Man Standing' strategy in lighting benefiting from competitor insolvency in Europe.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
